body:
`_probe_metadata_db()` in `cps/web.py` opens `metadata.db` and runs
`SELECT 1`.

`SELECT 1` is a constant expression. SQLite answers it without reading a page
of the database file, and `sqlite3.connect()` is lazy about opening the file
at all, so the probe can succeed against a database that is missing, corrupt,
truncated, or unreadable by the app user. It proves a connection object can be
constructed, not that the library is usable.

That is thin for the thing every Docker, Compose and Kubernetes deployment
polls to decide whether to route traffic or roll back.

`SELECT 1 FROM books LIMIT 1` would touch a real table and cost essentially
the same. Noted while fixing #1438 (#1459), which restored this probe to
working but deliberately did not redesign it.
title: Health check SELECT 1 never reads metadata.db, so a corrupt library probes healthy
